text:
Vincent Trocheck is 23 games into life with the Utah Mammoth after more than 300 with the Rangers, and André Tourigny is leaning on him harder by the week. His ice time over the last ten games is up more than four minutes a night to about 21, with 26 and 24 minutes in back-to-back overtime losses last week. He wins draws (the team even made a faceoff-win counter video about it) and he's been on the ice for good hockey: Utah takes 58.6% of the expected goals with him at five on five.

The scoring hasn't followed the role yet. He has 5 goals and 13 points, and he's about a goal and a half under his chances. Our talent range has his true rate a bit above where it sits now, and he's started to cash in, with a power-play goal against Vancouver and a goal and an assist against Colorado in his last two games.

Evolving-Hockey's read on last season is the caution: most of his value came on the power play, and his results ran ahead of his chances. Watch whether the five-on-five play holds up now that he's facing top lines for 21 minutes.
